feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for a senior digital communications/platform leader with clear public-sector positioning and solid evidence of progression, scope, and technical breadth. It reads polished and substantive, but it is slightly dense, somewhat repetitive across skills sections, and could sharpen impact by making outcomes more specific and trimming lower-value content.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear leadership narrative: strong progression within NACo and a well-defined niche in digital platforms, governance, analytics, and communications operations.  
- Good credibility signals: large-scale website migration, team/channel ownership, named tools, and quantified scope (10,000+ pages, 3.5M annual page views, 50+ publishers).  
- Writing is generally polished and professional, with consistent tone and strong use of action verbs.

1. Top improvements  
- Reduce duplication: “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT” overlap heavily. Consolidating these would improve structure and scannability.  
- Add more outcome-focused metrics beyond scope: include results such as engagement growth, efficiency gains, adoption, cost savings, or campaign performance.  
- Minor style/grammar consistency issues: “social, and multimedia” has an unnecessary comma; “Ranked among the top public universities…” is weak filler; “English (Native) French (A2/Learning)” needs separators for readability. Also standardize punctuation/hyphenation choices (e.g., AI-enabled, front-end, organization-wide) across sections.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible intro with clear seniority and public-sector focus, but it overlaps heavily with the subtitle, core competencies, and work experience. It would be stronger with one sharper value proposition and a few concrete signals of scope.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Tighten and reduce repetition: “Senior digital leader with 12+ years’ experience modernizing enterprise web platforms, governance, analytics, and content operations for high-volume public-sector communications.”
- Add clearer outcome/value language, e.g. “improving discoverability, publishing efficiency, and audience engagement across complex organizations.”
- Replace “Leads” with a parallel phrase tied to expertise: “Expertise spans web modernization, analytics infrastructure, editorial systems, multimedia production, and AI-enabled search/content experiences.”
- Consider aligning with the subtitle by emphasizing “platforms and communications systems” rather than listing every domain.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI-enabled user experiences” overlaps with core competencies and recent projects; “AI-enabled search/content experiences” would be more specific.
- The current intro repeats themes already covered in the subtitle and competencies block.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block overlaps heavily with the header and Topline Skills. It would be sharper if phrased more distinctly and tilted toward higher-level leadership capabilities rather than repeating detailed skill categories.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Tighten and standardize phrasing for parallel structure: Enterprise web modernization • Digital governance and editorial operations • Analytics, reporting, and insight infrastructure • Multi-channel communications leadership • AI-enabled search and content discovery • Workflow automation and platform integration • Public-sector advocacy communications • Multimedia and livestream production
- Consider replacing “website” with “web” for a more executive tone and cleaner wording.
- Change “content experiences” to “content discovery” or “user experiences” for greater specificity.
- Use “leadership” or “operations” selectively to emphasize senior scope, especially given Director-level experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Significant overlap with the header summary and all four Topline Skills blocks.
- “AI-enabled search,” “analytics infrastructure,” and “multimedia/livestream” are already reinforced in Recent Projects and Work Experience.
feedback.footer:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant project snapshot, but it largely repeats achievements already covered in recent roles and would be sharper with tighter phrasing, parallel structure, and clearer outcomes. The footer should complement the experience section, not restate it.

Suggested rewrite improvements
- Add a one-line lead-in such as “Selected recent projects” and keep all entries in parallel verb-led format.
- Tighten wording and improve consistency: “hybrid retrieval, vector search, and bill-level AI chat”; spell out “10 x 20-foot” consistently.
- Emphasize scope or value where possible: audience served, campaign purpose, or operational benefit (for example, “modular architecture for ongoing campaign expansion”).
- Consider this rewrite: “Selected Recent Projects: AI Hybrid Search—Designed a legislative search experience using hybrid retrieval, vector search, structured content workflows, and bill-level AI chat. We Are Counties Microsite—Built a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling, downloadable resources, and modular architecture for future growth. Organization Anniversary Campaign—Developed a multi-part digital campaign featuring editorial storytelling, archival media, web features, and a 10 x 20-foot interactive conference display. Advocacy Video Series—Produced a recurring advocacy video program spanning planning, production, and distribution across web, email, and social.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- AI Hybrid Search, microsite work, and advocacy video series closely overlap with the two most recent roles.
- The anniversary campaign may add the most distinct value because it is less explicitly covered elsewhere.

Leads enterprise web modernization, analytics infrastructure, editorial systems, multimedia production and AI-enabled user experiences for complex, mission-driven organizations.

items.title: Website
items.content: https://colemanpdavis.com/

items.title: Core Competencies
items.content: Enterprise website modernization • Digital governance & editorial systems • Analytics and reporting infrastructure • Multi-channel communications operations • AI-enabled search and content experiences • Workflow automation and platform integration • Advocacy and public-sector communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations

items.title: CV Footer
items.content:
### Recent Projects
**AI Hybrid Search**
Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience combining hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search and bill-level AI chat to improve discovery of complex policy content.
**We Are Counties Microsite**
Built a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, downloadable resources and a modular structure designed for continued campaign growth.
**Organization Anniversary Campaign**
Developed a multi-part digital campaign combining editorial storytelling, archival media, web features and a 10×20-foot interactive conference display connected to the main site.
**Advocacy Video Series**
Built a recurring advocacy video program spanning editorial planning, production and distribution across website, email and social channels.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant current role, but it reads as a task list and overlaps heavily with the header, skills, and Recent Projects. Tighten it around 3–4 high-impact contributions and add outcomes, scale, or scope where possible.

Suggested edit
- Open with impact + client scope: “Embedded full-time as strategic communications consultant for a U.S. national membership organization, leading digital platform improvements, campaign delivery, and content operations.”
- Consolidate overlapping bullets into sharper outcomes:
- “Built Drupal-based campaign and storytelling experiences, including modular microsites, reusable content components, and member-facing resource toolkits.”
- “Improved enterprise web operations by refining workflows, analytics, governance, and cross-channel publishing practices across web, email, social, and multimedia.”
- “Delivered front-end/CMS implementation and troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.”
- “Led an AI-enabled search initiative, defining retrieval strategy, structured content requirements, and discovery UX.”
- Add metrics if available: site size, traffic, number of publishers, campaign launches, time saved, search improvements.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- AI search and microsite examples already appear in Recent Projects; keep this entry higher-level and outcome-focused.
- Governance/analytics language also overlaps with the NACo Director role; emphasize what is new/current here.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact role with solid scale metrics; it should read more like an executive achievement entry and less like a responsibility summary. Emphasize transformation, team leadership, and business outcomes, while tightening channel-management bullets that overlap with earlier NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the opening with an outcome-led summary: “Directed NACo’s digital media function across web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget management, leading platform modernization and multi-channel communications for a national membership organization.”
- Tighten and prioritize the strongest bullets first: website migration, analytics stack expansion, and in-house studio build.
- Add measurable outcomes where possible: budget size, team size, email engagement growth, social growth, production volume, reporting efficiency, or time saved for publishers.
- Use stronger verbs and clearer impact framing, e.g., “Migrated 10,000+ pages to Drupal, improving governance for 50+ publishers and supporting 3.5M annual page views.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director role; either add distinct senior-level outcomes or cut it.
- Video-programming language overlaps with both earlier NACo roles and Recent Projects; keep the studio-build angle here.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this item overlaps heavily with the later Director role and earlier NACo role. Make it more clearly about execution, channel ownership, and systems-building at the manager-to-director transition level.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite the lead to emphasize scope and level: “Managed day-to-day multi-channel digital communications operations across NACo’s website, email, social media and advocacy video programs, supporting organization-wide editorial coordination.”
- Tighten and sharpen bullets: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Add clearer ownership and outcome language: “Launched and produced a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Reframe process bullets to show operational impact: “Built stronger editorial planning and cross-team coordination across communications, advocacy and program staff, improving publishing consistency and campaign alignment.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Digital publishing workflows” and “editorial coordination” overlap with the Director role’s governance/planning bullets.
- “Expanded a weekly advocacy video update” is close to the earlier NACo role and footer project; use “launched” or quantify growth if accurate.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this item overlaps heavily with the header and Core Competencies. It should be tightened to emphasize higher-level leadership strengths not already repeated elsewhere.

Suggested edit:
- Replace with more distinctive, outcome-oriented phrasing:
- Enterprise digital strategy for high-volume public-sector platforms
- Editorial governance and scalable publishing operations
- Cross-channel communications leadership across web, email, social and video
- Audience-centered content strategy for advocacy and member engagement
- Consider dropping “public-sector and advocacy messaging” in favor of “member engagement” or “organizational communications,” which feels more specific and less generic.
- Keep wording parallel: use noun phrases consistently and avoid mixing broad concepts with tactical activities.
- If space is tight, cut to 4 bullets; “audience-focused content planning” is the weakest and most duplicative.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy” and “editorial systems and governance” repeat the header/Core Competencies almost verbatim.
- “Multi-channel communications leadership” overlaps with multiple NACo roles; keep only if this section stays more strategic than operational.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it’s too tool-list-heavy and overlaps with both Core Competencies and Technical + IT. In Topline Skills, this should signal current strengths and execution scope, not repeat every platform.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from a software list to a capability-led line tied to recent work: “Drupal-focused web platforms, CMS modernization and front-end implementation.”
- Trim older/lower-priority items unless central to target roles; keep 5–7 items max.
- Group related skills for concision: “Drupal, WordPress, SharePoint & Power Pages” and “HTML/CSS/JavaScript, API integrations & workflow automation.”
- Suggested rewrite: “- Drupal-led web platforms - CMS modernization - Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery) - API integrations & workflow automation - Airtable systems - AI-enabled search experiences”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “CMS modernization,” “workflow automation,” and “AI-enabled search experiences” already appear in Core Competencies; vary wording or remove here.
- Platform/tool detail is already covered in Technical + IT, so avoid overloading this item with the same list.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tools list, but it reads as a generic inventory and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” analytics section. In Topline Skills, this should emphasize higher-level capability and decision-making impact, not repeat every platform.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tool list to capability-led phrasing: “Analytics strategy, KPI design, executive reporting, SEO/performance analysis.”
- Keep only the most differentiating tools: “GA4, BigQuery, Power BI/Looker Studio, Microsoft Clarity.”
- Tighten wording for seniority: replace “Leadership reporting” with “Executive dashboarding and decision support.”
- Suggested rewrite: “Analytics strategy and KPI design • Executive dashboarding and decision support • GA4, BigQuery, Power BI, Looker Studio, Microsoft Clarity • SEO and digital performance analysis”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This substantially duplicates “Technical + IT > Data, Analytics & Optimization”; use Topline Skills for strategic themes and leave full tool inventory there.
- “Analytics and reporting infrastructure” already appears in Core Competencies, so avoid repeating that exact phrasing.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong supporting skill area, but it reads generic and overlaps with “Multimedia production and livestream operations” in Core Competencies and several NACo bullets. Make it more senior, operational, and differentiated.

Suggested edit
- Reframe from task list to capability statement: “Broadcast-quality video production • Livestream and hybrid event delivery • PTZ camera and studio system operation • Virtual event production workflows”
- Consider emphasizing leadership/operations over hands-on basics: replace “video production and editing” with “studio production and multimedia operations” if targeting senior roles.
- If accurate, add scale or context to increase credibility: “broadcast-quality,” “in-house studio,” or “recurring advocacy programming.”
- Keep terms parallel and concise; avoid mixing tools (“PTZ camera systems”) with broad functions unless all bullets are similarly scoped.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Livestreaming” duplicates Core Competencies (“Multimedia production and livestream operations”); vary wording or remove one mention.
- “Studio operations” and “hybrid/virtual event production” are already evidenced in recent NACo roles, so this skills line should summarize rather than repeat.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it’s too bare and duplicates the stronger “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” section. This item should either be tightened to emphasize depth/relevance or removed to avoid repeating the same keywords.

Suggested edit:
- Reorder by strongest/recent relevance: “Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages” is fine, but consider adding level/context: “Drupal (enterprise/public-sector), WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages, GitHub Pages.”
- If space allows, make it outcome-oriented rather than just a list: “CMS platforms: Drupal (10,000+ page migration; microsites), WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages, GitHub Pages.”
- Use this section to show platform specialization, not generic repetition; Drupal should clearly lead given recent roles and projects.
- Keep naming consistent with the rest of the CV: use “CMS platforms” or “Web platforms” consistently across sections.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This substantially overlaps with Topline Skills [2]; consider deleting one version or differentiating this item by adding proficiency/context.
- GitHub Pages may feel lightweight versus enterprise platforms unless tied to a specific use case.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant stack, but it reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. Tighten it to emphasize implementation tools that support recent Drupal, analytics, automation, and AI/search work.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Front-End & Technical Implementation
- Rewrite as: JavaScript, HTML5, CSS3, jQuery • API and tag integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions/CI workflows
- Consider grouping by function rather than listing everything flat: Front-end (HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, jQuery) | Integration & deployment (APIs, GTM, Cloudflare Workers, GitHub Actions)
- If accurate, add scope/outcome in adjacent experience bullets instead of here, e.g., “built custom Drupal components,” “deployed automation via GitHub Actions,” or “implemented tag/API integrations supporting analytics/search.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” already appear under Topline Skills; avoid repeating the same phrasing in both places.
- GTM also overlaps conceptually with analytics infrastructure in recent roles; keep this section tool-focused, not impact-focused.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow systems capability. It also overlaps with “Workflow automation and platform integration” in Core Competencies and “Airtable systems / Workflow automation” in Topline Skills.

Suggested edit
- Reframe from a pure list to grouped systems that signal use case: “Workflow automation & work management: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier, Jira, Asana, Trello, Basecamp.”
- Move collaboration tools out of this item if space allows: Slack, Teams belong better under a broader “Collaboration Tools” line or can be dropped.
- If accurate, add a short qualifier to show impact: “Used to build editorial planning systems, automate approvals/notifications, and coordinate cross-team delivery.”
- Consider ordering by strongest/recently used tools first: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier, Jira, Asana, Trello, Basecamp.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Airtable” and “workflow automation” already appear in Topline Skills/Core Competencies; avoid repeating the same phrasing.
- Slack and Teams are low-value here unless tied to automation/integration use.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant tools, but this line is too bare compared with the rest of the CV and misses the scale/ownership implied by recent email leadership. Make it more specific and aligned to enterprise communications operations.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Email Marketing, CRM & Member Engagement Platforms
- Rewrite as: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic Thrive • Mailchimp
- If accurate, add scope in parentheses to show level: enterprise email automation, newsletter operations, audience segmentation
- Consider ordering by strongest/recentest platform first based on actual use; if Higher Logic was primary at NACo, list it before Mailchimp

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item overlaps with work-experience bullets about newsletters and digital channel leadership; avoid repeating outcomes here unless you remove them from older roles
- “Engagement Systems” is vague and partially duplicates “Automation & Workflow Systems”; clarify this is specifically email/CRM platforms

items.title: Data, Analytics & Optimization
items.content: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • Looker Studio • Power BI • BigQuery • SEO • A/B testing • Dashboarding
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this item is highly duplicative of “Topline Skills > Analytics, Insights & Optimization” and reads as a generic list rather than a differentiated technical stack. Tighten it and emphasize methods/tools not already stated elsewhere.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Data & Optimization Tools
- Rewrite as: GA4 • BigQuery • Power BI • Looker Studio • Microsoft Clarity • Google Search Console • A/B testing • KPI reporting
- Replace “Dashboarding” with a more specific capability like “KPI reporting” or “performance analysis.”
- If accurate, add one stronger technical item such as “data visualization,” “event tracking,” or “tagging strategy” instead of broad “SEO.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely repeats the “Topline Skills” analytics section almost verbatim; consider deleting one version or making this section tools-only while leaving strategy in Topline Skills.
- GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery are already reinforced in the recent Director role, so avoid overloading this list with generic terms.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but the item is too broad and overlaps with the 2018–2024 NACo roles. Make it read as an early-career foundation role focused on team formation, production, and workflow support.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to emphasize scope and progression: “Promoted across two digital roles while helping establish NACo’s first in-house digital team.”
- Split into 2 concise bullets focused on distinct contributions:
- “Supported digital operations across web, email, social and multimedia, helping formalize early publishing workflows and cross-channel coordination.”
- “Contributed to a major website refresh and produced recurring digital content, including livestreams and weekly video updates; provided day-to-day direction to a digital media associate.”
- If possible, add metrics: number of livestreams/videos produced, audience reach, publishing volume, or efficiency gains from workflow improvements.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; keep this item framed as launching/supporting the format, not leading or scaling it.
- Avoid repeating broad “strengthened workflows” language already used in later NACo entries unless tied to a specific outcome.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry that shows the start of your multimedia and innovation work, but it reads generic and overlaps with later NACo roles. Emphasize the podcast launch as the clearest differentiator and trim broad duties.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to foreground the unique achievement: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting NACo program and policy teams; launched the organization’s first podcast, leading concept development, scripting and production.”
- Replace “contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials” with a more specific phrase like “produced digital and multimedia content for program and policy communications.”
- If possible, add scope or output: number of episodes, audiences served, cross-functional partners, or examples of research/projects supported.
- Keep this entry concise since later NACo roles already show broader digital leadership.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Digital content production and multimedia materials” overlaps with the 2015–2018 Digital Media Manager / Producer role.
- Avoid repeating general coordination language already covered by later editorial and cross-department planning entries.

items.title: Multimedia & Creative Tools
items.content: Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Livestream studio workflows • Podcast production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid supporting skills, but this item mixes software with capabilities and repeats multimedia themes already covered in Core Competencies and Topline Skills. Tighten it to emphasize tools only, with the strongest, most current production capabilities implied elsewhere.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Creative & Audio/Video Tools
